conditions.label: ENTAILMENT

quote_checks.quote: Since DART’s intentional collision with Dimorphos on Sept. 26, astronomers have been using telescopes on Earth to measure how much that time has changed.
quote_checks.label: ENTAILMENT
quote_checks.reason: This directly states that DART collided with Dimorphos, satisfying actual impact.

conditions.reason: The cited NASA passage expressly says DART had an intentional collision with Dimorphos.

conditions.label: ENTAILMENT

quote_checks.quote: Before its encounter, NASA had defined a minimum successful orbit period change of Dimorphos as change of 73 seconds or more.
quote_checks.label: ENTAILMENT
quote_checks.reason: This establishes the pre-impact success threshold of at least 73 seconds.

quote_checks.quote: Now, the investigation team has confirmed the spacecraft’s impact altered Dimorphos’ orbit around Didymos by 32 minutes, shortening the 11 hour and 55-minute orbit to 11 hours and 23 minutes. This measurement has a margin of uncertainty of approximately plus or minus 2 minutes.
quote_checks.label: ENTAILMENT
quote_checks.reason: A 32-minute change, even allowing for ±2 minutes, remains far above 73 seconds.

quote_checks.quote: Over the following weeks, the asteroid’s orbital period continued to shorten as Dimorphos lost more rocky material to space, finally settling at 11 hours, 22 minutes, and 3 seconds per orbit – 33 minutes and 15 seconds less time than before impact. This calculation is accurate to within 1 1⁄2 seconds, Naidu said.
quote_checks.label: ENTAILMENT
quote_checks.reason: This later measured change is also far above 73 seconds and further confirms the threshold was exceeded.

conditions.reason: NASA’s stated success criterion was 73 seconds or more, and the cited post-impact measurements show a shortening of 32 minutes, later 33 minutes 15 seconds, both decisively above that threshold.
